main_text.p: congruum producit, ȷ 4 grad. 4 s scrup.Lecnis.

Tertio, quando neuter eorum numerorum qui exhibentur, definitè exacteq; continetur in tabulis, locū ecliptice respondentem arcui æquatoris hac uia exploramus. Sit ascensio data ııs grad. sı scru. locus ecliptice huic congruens sit indagandus in regione cui polus sı grad. so scrup. erigitur. Neuter expresse in tabulis numerus habetur. Inquisitionem ergo hoc modo instituimus.

Ad latitudinem s ı grad. ascensioni proxime minori respondet ȷ4 gradus Leonis, estq; proxime minor ascensio ȷ ȷ 4 grad. 4 s. proxime maior ȷ ȷ 6 grad. ȷ ꝛ scrup. Differentia prima s 8 grad. Differentia secunda minoris ascensionis & oblatæ 64 scrup. pars proportionalis ergo 4s scrup. Et uerus ecliptice locus datæ ascensioni conueniens polo, sı grad. integris elato, in ȷ4 grad. 4s scrup. Leonis incidit. Ad latitudinem uero s2 grad. ascensioni proxime minori ȷs Leonis ex aduerso respondet, estq; minor ascensio ȷȷs grad. 23 scrup. proxime maior ȷȷ6 grad. 46 scrup. Differentia prima 86 scrup. Differentia secunda ascensionis minoris & datæ 28 scrup. pars proportionalis hinc competens 19 scrupulorum. quæ addita ıs grad. 19 scrup. Leonis, uerum ecliptice locum ad datam ascensionem in hoc situ sphæræ producunt.

page.notes: Old-style numerals in the text (ȷ, ı, ȷȷ, s) are the printed ligatured forms for the degrees and scruples; their exact values are uncertain and rendered approximately. The catchword "Cum" at the lower right is set as the start of the next section's initial and is given as the final line. Greek or Hebrew: none.
